72.text:
Assertion : Tapeworm, roundworm and pinworm are endoparasites of human intestine.
Reason : Improperly cooked food is the source of all intestinal infections.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
72.sol: Tapeworm belonging to Phylum Platyhelminthes, pinworms and roundworm belonging to Phylum Nematoda, are all endoparasites. They all are intestinal parasites. In case of Taenia solium man gets infection by uncooked or improperly cooked measly pork. Cysticercus becomes active on reaching the intestine. Proscolex everts or evaginates in the intestinal wall. Ascaris, being an endoparasite inhabits the small intestine of man, more frequently of children than of adults. Man gets infection through skin contact. Enterobius vermicularis or pinworm lives in caecum, appendix and at the junction of large and small intestine. It is transmitted by the improper sanitary condition.

3149.text: The time required for a first order reaction to complete $90 \%$ is ' $t$ '. What is the time required to complete $99 \%$ of the same reaction?
3149.sol:
For the first order reaction,
$t=\frac{2303}{k} \log \frac{a}{a-x}$
Now putting the values
$\begin{aligned}
& t_{90 \%}=t=\frac{2303}{k} \log \left(\frac{100}{100-90}\right) \\
& t_{99 \%}=\frac{2303}{k} \log \left(\frac{100}{100-99}\right) \\
& \frac{t}{t_{99 \%}}=\frac{\frac{2303}{k} \log \left(\frac{100}{10}\right)}{\frac{2303}{k} \log \left(\frac{100}{1}\right)}=\frac{1}{2} \\
& t_{99 \%}=2 t
\end{aligned}$

6700.text: The coefficient of $x^3 y^4 z^5$ in the expansion of $(x y+y z+x z)^6$ is
6700.sol:
We have
$\begin{aligned}
(x y+y z+z x)^6 & =\sum_{r+s+t=6} \frac{6 !}{r ! s ! t !}(x y)^r(y z)^s(z x)^t \\
& =\sum_{r+s+t=6} \frac{6 !}{r ! s ! t !} x^{r+t} y^{r+s} z^{s+t}
\end{aligned}$
If the general term in the above expansion. contains $x^3 y^4 z^5$, then
$r+t=3, r+s=4 \text{$ and } s+t=5
Also, $r+s+t=6$
Solving these equations, we get
$r=1, s=3, t=2\therefore$ Coefficient of
$x^3 y^4 z^5=\frac{6 !}{1 ! 3 ! 2 !}=\frac{6 !}{2 ! 3 !}=60$

10724.sol:
Let winning probability of C be P(C) = p
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad P(A)=P(B)=2 p \\ & \because \quad P(A)+P(B)+P(C)=1 \\ & 2 p+2 p+p=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 5 p=1 \\ & p=1 / 5 \\ & \end{aligned}\therefore$ Probability that $B or C$ win $=P(B)+P(C)=2 p+p[\because B$ and C are mutually exclusive events $]$
=3 p=$\frac{3}{5}$

11844.sol:
$x^{\frac{2}{3}}+y^{\frac{2}{3}}=a^{\frac{2}{3}}\qquad ....\mathrm{(i)}$ Any point on (i) is $\left(a \cos ^3 \theta, a \sin ^3 \theta\right)$ Slope of tangent $=-\tan \theta$ Equation of the tangent is : $\begin{aligned} & y-a \sin ^3 \theta=-\tan \theta\left(x-a \cos ^3 \theta\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x \sin \theta+y \cos \theta=\frac{a}{2} \sin 2 \theta \qquad ....\mathrm{(ii)} \end{aligned}$
Slope of normal $=\cot \theta$ Equation of normal is : $y-a \sin ^3 \theta=\cot \theta\left(x-a \cos ^3 \theta\right)\Rightarrow x \cos \theta-y \sin \theta=a \cos 2 \theta $
Now, $p_1=\left|\frac{-a \sin \theta \cos \theta}{\sqrt{\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta}}\right|=\frac{a}{2} \sin 2 \theta\Rightarrow 2 p_1=a \sin 2 \theta \qquad ....\mathrm{(iii)}$ and $p_2=\left|\frac{-a \cos 2 \theta}{\sqrt{\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta}}\right|=a \cos 2 \theta\Rightarrow p_2=a \cos 2 \theta$
Squaring and adding (iii) and (iv) $\begin{aligned} & 4 p_1^2+p_2^2=a^2 \\ & \Rightarrow k_1=4, k_2=1 \Rightarrow k_1+k_2=5 \end{aligned}$

13756.text: A $4 \mu \mathrm{F}$ capacitor is charged by a $200 \mathrm{ V}$ battery. It is then disconnected from the supply and is connected to another uncharged $2 \mu \mathrm{F}$ capacitor. During the process, loss of energy (in $\mathrm{J}$ ) is
13756.sol:
Charge stored at the capacitor
$q=C_1 V_1=4 \times 200=800 \mu \mathrm{C}$
When this capacitor is connected with a uncharged capacitor, then common potential on both capacitors
$V=\frac{C_1 V_1+C_2 V_2}{C_1+C_2}=\frac{800+0}{4+2}=\frac{800}{6} \mathrm{ V}$
Loss in energy = Initial energy - Final energy
$\begin{aligned}
= & \frac{1}{2} C_1 V_1^2-\frac{1}{2}\left(C_1+C_2\right) V^2 \\
= & \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 10^{-6} \times(200)^2 \\
& \quad-\frac{1}{2}(4+2) \times 10^{-6} \times\left(\frac{800}{6}\right)^2 \\
= & 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^4-\frac{3 \times 10^{-6} \times 64 \times 10^4}{36} \\
= & 8 \times 10^{-2}-\frac{64}{12} \times 10^{-2} \\
= & 8 \times 10^{-2}-5.33 \times 10^{-2} \\
= & 2.67 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ J}
\end{aligned}$

13799.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
13799.text: Ball $A$ of mass $1 \mathrm{ kg}$ moving along a straight line with a velocity of $4 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ hits another ball $B$ of mass $3 \mathrm{ kg}$ which is at rest. After collision, they stick together and move with the same velocity along the same straight line. If the time of impact of the collision is $0.1 \mathrm{ s}$ then the force exerted on $B$ is
13799.sol:
For ball A$,
\begin{aligned} & m_A=1 \mathrm{ kg}, v_A=4 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1} \\ & \text{$ for $ball } B, m_B=3 \mathrm{ kg}, v_B=0\end{aligned}\therefore$ Total momentum before collision,
$\begin{aligned} p_i & =m_A v_A+m_B v_B \\ & =1 \times 4+3 \times 0=4 \mathrm{ kg}-\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}\end{aligned}$
Since, after collision, both body stick together, therefore, it is the case of perfectly enelastic collision. Let $v$ be the common velocity, then total momentum after collision,
$\begin{aligned} p_f & =\left(m_A+m_B\right) v \\ & =(1+3) v=4 v\end{aligned}$
According to law of conservation of linear momentum,
$p_i=p_f\Rightarrow \quad 4=4 v \Rightarrow v=1 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1} 
Time of impact, $\Delta t=0.1 $\mathrm{ s}$
Force exerted on the body $B$,
$F_B=\frac{\Delta p_B}{\Delta t}=\frac{m_B\left(v_B-u_B\right)$}{\Delta t}=$\frac{3(v-0)}{01}$\Rightarrow \quad F_B=$\frac{3(1-0)}{01}=\frac{3}{01}=30 \mathrm{ N}$

15332.sol:
Using parallelogram law of vector addition,

Resultant force acting on object is ${F}_{R} = \sqrt{{F}_{1}^{2} + {F}_{2}^{2} + 2{F}_{1}{F}_{2}cos\theta}$, here, $\theta = 90 ° - 30 ° = 60 °$ is angle between the forces.

Putting the values, we have

${F}_{R} = \sqrt{{4}^{2} + {4}^{2} + 2\left(4\right)\left(4\right)cos60 °} = 6. 9N$

Acceleration of the object is $a = \dfrac{FR}{m} = \dfrac{6. 9}{1} = 6. 9ms^{- 2}$.

19487.subject: Chemistry
19487.text:
What are the intermediates formed during the reactions A and B ?
A. Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
B. Dehydration of alcohols in the slow rate determining step.
19487.sol:
A. Reimer-Tiemann Reaction:
Phenol is treated with $CHCl_3$ and $NaOH$. The base generates dichlorocarbene $(:CCl_2)$, which attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion. The intermediate is sodium 2-(dichloromethyl)phenolate — a phenoxide ring with an ortho $-CHCl_2$ group (option 4, structure A).

B. Dehydration of Alcohols (slow step):
In acid-catalyzed E1 dehydration, the slow rate-determining step is the breaking of the C$-$O bond after protonation of $-OH$, forming a carbocation $R^+$. The intermediate is the carbocation $H_3C-\overset{(+)}{C}-H$ (option 4, structure B).

Option (4) is correct.

20224.text:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: Heterocyclic compounds like Pyridine and Thiophene are non-aromatic compounds.
Reason: According to Huckel rule for a given compound to exhibit aromaticity, the molecule must be planar, cyclic system having delocalised $(4 n+2) \pi$ electrons.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct.
Reason is correct but Assertion is incorrect.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect.
20224.sol:
Assertion is incorrect: Pyridine and Thiophene are well-known aromatic compounds. Pyridine has 6 delocalized $\pi$ electrons (3 double bonds), and Thiophene has 6 delocalized $\pi$ electrons (2 double bonds + lone pair of S). Both satisfy Huckel's rule and are aromatic.

Reason is correct: Huckel's rule states that a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with $(4n+2)\pi$ electrons is aromatic.

Reason is correct but Assertion is incorrect.

21082.subject: Mathematics
21082.text: The coefficient of the third term in the expansion of $\left(x^2-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^n$, when expanded in the descending power of $x$ is 31, then $n$ is
21082.sol:
The general term in the expansion of $(x^2 - \dfrac{1}{4})^n$ is given by $T_{r+1} = ^{n}C_{r} (x^2)^{n-r} (-\dfrac{1}{4})^r$.

The third term corresponds to $r = 2$.

$T_{3} = ^{n}C_{2} (x^2)^{n-2} (-\dfrac{1}{4})^2 = ^{n}C_{2} x^{2n-4} (\dfrac{1}{16})$.

The coefficient of the third term is given as 31. Since the expansion is in descending powers of $x$, the coefficient is independent of $x$ if $2n-4 = 0$, but here the coefficient is simply the constant part of the term.

The coefficient is $\dfrac{^{n}C_{2}}{16} = 31$.

Therefore, ^{n}C_{2} = 31 \times 16 = 496$.

Using the formula ^{n}C_{2} = \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$, we have $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2} = 496$.

$n(n-1) = 992$.

Solving $n^2 - n - 992 = 0$ using the quadratic formula $n = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4(1)(-992)}}{2} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 3968}}{2} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{3969}}{2}$.

Since $\sqrt{3969} = 63$, $n = \dfrac{1 + 63}{2} = 32$.

Answer: 32

21616.sol:
The expression is $E = \operatorname{cosec}^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right) + \sec^{-1}(2) + \cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$.

Simplify each term:
1. $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
2. $\tan^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
3. $\sec^{-1}(2) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
4. $\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \pi - \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.
5. $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Summing these values:
$E = -\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$E = -\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Finding a common denominator of 12:
$E = \dfrac{-2\pi + 8\pi - 3\pi}{12} = \dfrac{3\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

21832.subject: Mathematics
21832.text: The number of words that can be formed with the letters of the word 'DEFINITE' if two vowels are together and the other two are also together but separated from the first two is
21832.sol:
DEFINITE has 8 letters: Consonants: D, F, N, T (4 distinct); Vowels: E, E, I, I (4 letters with repetition).

The condition requires two groups of 2 vowels each, separated by at least one consonant.

Arrange 4 consonants: $4! = 24$ ways, creating 5 gaps: $\_C\_C\_C\_C\_$

Choose 2 gaps (separated) for the two vowel groups: $\binom{5}{2} = 10$ ways

Arrange 4 vowels (E, E, I, I) in the 4 slots: $\dfrac{4!}{2! \cdot 2!} = \dfrac{24}{4} = 6$ ways

Total $= 24 \times 10 \times 6 = 1440$

22980.subject: Physics
22980.text: A balloon with mass $m$ is descending down with an acceleration $a$ (where, $a < g$ ). How much mass should be removed from it so that it starts moving up with an acceleration $a$ ?
22980.sol:
Let $F$ be the upward buoyant force acting on the balloon. When the balloon of mass $m$ is descending with acceleration $a$, the equation of motion is $mg - F = ma$.

From this, $F = m(g - a)$.

Let $m'$ be the mass to be removed, so the new mass is $m - m'$. When the balloon moves up with acceleration $a$, the equation of motion is $F - (m - m')g = (m - m')a$.

Substituting $F = m(g - a)$ into the equation, we get $m(g - a) - (m - m')g = (m - m')a$.

$mg - ma - mg + m'g = ma - m'a$.

$m'g + m'a = 2ma$.

$m'(g + a) = 2ma$.

$m' = \dfrac{2ma}{g + a}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2 m a}{g+a}$

23480.subject: Physics
23480.text: An ideal diode is connected in series with a capacitor. The free ends of the capacitor and the diode are connected across a $220 \mathrm{ V}$ ac source. Now the potential difference across the capacitor is :
23480.sol:
The input voltage is an AC source given by $V(t) = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$, where $V_{rms} = 220 \text{ V}$. The peak voltage $V_0$ is given by $V_0 = V_{rms} \sqrt{2} = 220 \sqrt{2} \approx 311 \text{ V}$.

The circuit consists of an ideal diode in series with a capacitor. During the positive half-cycle of the AC source, the diode is forward-biased and acts as a short circuit. The capacitor charges up to the peak value of the input voltage, which is $V_0 = 311 \text{ V}$.

During the negative half-cycle, the diode becomes reverse-biased and acts as an open circuit. Since the diode prevents the discharge of the capacitor, the capacitor retains its charge and remains at the peak potential difference of $311 \text{ V}$.

Therefore, the potential difference across the capacitor is $311 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $311 \mathrm{ V}$

24229.subject: Mathematics
24229.text: Let $l_1$ be the line joining $(1, 1, 1)$ and $(3, 1, 3)$ and let $l_2$ be the line joining $(0, 2, -1)$ and $(2, 0, 3)$. What is the angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$?
24229.sol:
Direction ratios of line $l_1$ joining $(1, 1, 1)$ and $(3, 1, 3)$ are $(3-1, 1-1, 3-1) = (2, 0, 2)$.

Direction ratios of line $l_2$ joining $(0, 2, -1)$ and $(2, 0, 3)$ are $(2-0, 0-2, 3-(-1)) = (2, -2, 4)$.

Let $\theta$ be the angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$. Using the formula for the angle between two lines with direction ratios $(a_1, b_1, c_1)$ and $(a_2, b_2, c_2)$:

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|a_1 a_2 + b_1 b_2 + c_1 c_2|}{\sqrt{a_1^2 + b_1^2 + c_1^2} \sqrt{a_2^2 + b_2^2 + c_2^2}}$

Substituting the values:

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|(2)(2) + (0)(-2) + (2)(4)|}{\sqrt{2^2 + 0^2 + 2^2} \sqrt{2^2 + (-2)^2 + 4^2}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|4 + 0 + 8|}{\sqrt{8} \sqrt{24}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{12}{2\sqrt{2} \times 2\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{12}{8\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\theta = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$

Answer: $30^o$

All rays with the angle of incidence $i$ less than a particular value $i_{m}$ are confined in the medium of refractive index $n_{1}$. The numerical aperture (NA) of the structure is defined as $\sin i_{m}$.

Question: If two structures of same cross-sectional area, but different numerical apertures $N A_{1}$ and $N A_{2}\left(N A_{2} < N A_{1}\right)$ are joined longitudinally, the numerical aperture of the combined structure is

It is given that $N{A}_{2} < N{A}_{1}$
$⇒ {{i}_{m}}_{2} < {{i}_{m}}_{1}$
Hence if the combination can be placed both ways i.e. ${1}^{st}$ structure & then ${2}^{nd}$ structure and then reversed also, then the condition of TIR is satisfied for lower ${i}_{m}$ then it can be satisfied for all other less angles as well.
Hence $N{A}_{2}$ will be the numerical aperture of the combined structure.

26595.text: A horizontal force $F$ is applied at the centre of mass of a cylindrical object of mass $m$ and radius $R$, perpendicular to its axis as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between the object and the ground is $\mu$. The centre of mass of the object has an acceleration $a$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. Given that the object rolls without slipping, which of the following statement(s) is (are) correct?
options: For the same $F$, the value of $a$ does not depend on whether the cylinder is solid or hollow.
For a solid cylinder, the maximum possible value of $a$ is $2\mug$.
The magnitude of the frictional force on the object due to the ground is always $\mumg$.
26595.sol:
Let moment of inertia $= I$

For pure rolling, $a = \alphaR$

and $F - f = ma . . . \left(1\right)$

and $fR = I\alpha$

or $fR = \dfrac{Ia}{R}$

or $f = \dfrac{Ia}{{R}^{2}}$

Therefore, $F - \dfrac{Ia}{{R}^{2}} = ma$

$∴ F = \left(m + \dfrac{I}{{R}^{2}}\right)a$

$⇒$ For the same value of $F$, value of $a$ depends on $I$.

$⇒$ For a solid cylinder$\left(I = \dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2}\right)$ (to calculate maximum $a$)

$f = \mumg$

$∴ \mumg = \left(\dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{2}\right) \times \dfrac{a}{{R}^{2}}$

Therefore, $a = 2\mug$

$⇒ f$ is dependent on applied force.

$⇒$ For thin-walled hollow cylinder$\left(I = m{R}^{2}\right)$,

$F = \left(m + \dfrac{m{R}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}\right)a = 2ma$

$∴ a = \dfrac{F}{2m}$

28821.subject: Chemistry
28821.text: Low oxidation state of metals in their complexes are common when ligands
28821.sol:
When metal has low oxidation state, it has more electron density in d orbital. So it has more tendency to back donate electrons. Thus compound must have good $\pi$ acceptor ligand.

π backbonding, also called π backdonation, is when electrons move from an atomic orbital on one atom to an appropriate symmetry antibonding orbital on a π-acceptor ligand.It is especially common in the organometallic chemistry of transition metals with multi-atomic ligands such as carbon monoxide, ethylene or the nitrosonium cation. Electrons from the metal are used to bond to the ligand, in the process relieving the metal of excess negative charge. Compounds where π backbonding occurs include $Ni ( CO{)}_{4}$ and Zeise's salt.

The metal to ligand bonding creates a synergic effect which strengthens the bond between ligand and the metal

30100.text: In liquation process used for tin $\left(Sn\right)$, the metal
options: is brought to molten form which is made to flow on a slope
30100.sol:
Liquation is a metallurgical method for separating metals from an ore or alloy.

This method was largely used to remove lead containing silver from copper, but it can also be used to remove antimony minerals from ore, and refine tin.

Liquation process is used for metal having low melting point such as tin in which they are heated and brought to molten state and made to flow down the slope while impurities with higher melting point left on the top.

Liquation is similar to distillation, except instead of vaporizing the impure metal, it is melted.

34241.sol:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}\left(f\left(t\right)\right)\right)}^{2}}dt = e . . . \left(1\right)$

Put $x = 0$, then

$f\left(0\right) = e$.

Differentiating $\left(1\right)$ w.r.t. $x$, we get

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right)\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}\left(f\left(x\right)\right)\right)}^{2}} = 0$

Put $y = f\left(x\right)$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}^{2}}} = - ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}{\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}^{2}}} = - ∫ dx$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left({\log}_{e}y\right) = - x + C$

Put $x = 0, y = e$

$\sin^{- 1}\left({\log}_{e}e\right) = - 0 + C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

So,

$\sin^{- 1}\left({\log}_{e}y\right) = - x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}y = sin\left(- x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}f\left(x\right) = sin\left(- x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Put $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = sin\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ 6{\log}_{e}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 3\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ {\left\{6{\log}_{e}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right\}}^{2} = 27$

35736.text: Let $f\left(x\right)$ be a polynomial function such that $f\left(x\right) + {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = {x}^{5} + 64$. Then, the value of $\lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x - 1}$ is equal to
35736.sol:
Let $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{4} + a{x}^{3} + b{x}^{2} + cx + d\right)$

$f\left(x\right) + {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + {f}^{''}\left(x\right) = {x}^{5} + \left(a + 4\right){x}^{4} + \left(b + 3a + 16\right){x}^{3} +$

$\left(9a + 2b + c - 12\right){x}^{2} + \left(d + c + 4b - 6a\right)x + \left(c - 2b\right)$

$∵ f\left(x\right) + {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + {f}^{''}\left(x\right) = {x}^{5} + 64$

$⇒ a + 4 = 0, b + 3a + 16 = 0, 9a + 2b + c - 12 = 0, d + c + 4b - 6a = 0$

$⇒ a = - 4, b = - 4, c = 56, d = - 64$

So $\lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x - 1} = \lim_{x \to 1}\left({x}^{4} - 4{x}^{3} - 4{x}^{2} + 56x - 64\right)$

$= 1 - 4 - 4 + 56 - 64 = - 15$

36028.text: Let $\left[\begin{array}{ll}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 2 \\ - 1\end{array} \begin{array}{ll}0 \\ - 1 \\ 2\end{array}$\right]$. If \left|adj ( adj\left(adj2A )\right)\right| = ( 16{)}^{n}$, then $n$ is equal to
36028.sol:
Given that $A = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & - 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 2\end{cases}\right]$ and $\left|adj\left(adj\left(adj2A\right)\right)\right| = {16}^{n}$.

We know that $\left|adjA\right| = {\left|A\right|}^{n - 1}$ and $\left|adj\left(adjA\right)\right| = {\left|A\right|}^{{\left(n - 1\right)}^{2}}$

Similarly, $\left|adj\left(adj\left(adjA\right)\right)\right| = {\left|A\right|}^{{\left(n - 1\right)}^{3}}$ where $n$ is the order of the square matrix.

Let us find $\left|A\right|$.

$\left|A\right| = 2\left(2 \times 2 - \left(- 1\right)\left(- 1\right)\right) - 1\left(1 \times 2 - 0\left(- 1\right)\right) + 0\left(1 \times \left(- 1\right) - 0 \times 2\right)$

$= 2\left(3\right) - \left(2\right) + 0 = 4$

$⇒ {\left|2A\right|}^{{\left(n - 1\right)}^{3}} = {\left|2A\right|}^{{\left(3 - 1\right)}^{3}}$

$= {\left|2A\right|}^{8} = {\left({2}^{8}\right)}^{3}{\left|A\right|}^{8}$

$⇒ {2}^{24} \times {4}^{8} = {16}^{n}$

$⇒ {16}^{6} \times {16}^{4} = {16}^{n}$

$⇒ {16}^{10} = {16}^{n}$

$⇒ n = 10$

Therefore, the value of $n$ is $10$.

36054.text: Let $A = \left(\begin{cases}4 & - 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right)$. If ${A}^{2} + \gammaA + 18I = O$, then $det \left(A\right)$ is equal to _______.
36054.sol:
Given $A = \left[\begin{cases}4 & - 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right] ⇒ det\left(A\right) = 4\beta + 2\alpha$

Characteristic equation of the matrix is

$\left[\begin{cases}4 - \lambda & - 2 \\ \alpha & \beta - \lambda\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ 4\beta + {\lambda}^{2} - \left(\beta + 4\right)\lambda + 2\alpha = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} - \left(\beta + 4\right)\lambda + 2\alpha + 4\beta = 0$

Comparing with given equation ${A}^{2} + \gammaA + 18I = 0$, we get

$⇒ \gamma = - \left(\beta + 4\right) \text{$ and $} 2\alpha + 4\beta = 18$

Hence $det \left(A\right) = 4\beta + 2\alpha = 18$

39517.subject: Physics
39517.text: Which one of the following is not a measurable quantity?
39517.sol:
In electrostatics and circuit theory, potential (voltage) at a single point is defined relative to a reference point (usually infinity or ground where potential is assumed to be zero).
Absolute voltage at a point is not a physically measurable quantity because only the difference in potential between two points can be measured using instruments like a voltmeter.
Resistance can be measured using an ohmmeter or bridge circuits.
Displacement current is a physical quantity that can be calculated and its effects (magnetic field) can be measured.
Voltage difference (potential difference) is the standard quantity measured between two points in a circuit.
Therefore, absolute voltage is not a measurable quantity.

40284.text:
An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, $\sigma=10 \mathrm{mho} / \mathrm{m}$. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is $\_\_\_\_$.
$\left[\text{Take }\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{\mathrm{o}}}=9 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{Nm}^{2} / \mathrm{C}^{2}\right]$
40284.sol:
For an electromagnetic wave in a conducting medium, the maximum conduction current density is $J_{c,max} = \sigma E_0$ and maximum displacement current density is $J_{d,max} = \epsilon_0 \omega E_0$.
The ratio is: $\frac{J_{c,max}}{J_{d,max}} = \frac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0 \omega}$.
With $\sigma = 10$ mho/m, $f = 100$ MHz
So $\omega = 2\pi \times 10^8$ rad/s, and $\epsilon_0 = \frac{10^{-9}}{36\pi}$ F/m: $\frac{J_{c,max}}{J_{d,max}} = \frac{10 \times 36\pi}{10^{-9} \times 2\pi \times 10^8} = \frac{10 \times 36}{2 \times 10^{-1}} = 1800$.

40431.text: Two point charges $q_1=3\,\mu C$ and $q_2=-4\,\mu C$ are placed at points $(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+3\hat{k})$ and $(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ respectively. Force on charge $q_2$ is ________ N. $\left(\text{Take } \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times 10^9 \text{ SI Units}\right)$
40431.sol:
Position vector of $q_1$, $\vec{r}_1 = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$

Position vector of $q_2$, $\vec{r}_2 = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$

Vector from $q_1$ to $q_2$ is $\vec{r}_{21} = \vec{r}_2 - \vec{r}_1 = (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) - (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$

Magnitude $|\vec{r}_{21}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + (-2)^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3$

Force on $q_2$ due to $q_1$ is given by Coulomb's law in vector form:

$\vec{F}_{21} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{|\vec{r}_{21}|^3} \vec{r}_{21}$

Substituting the given values:

$\vec{F}_{21} = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times (3 \times 10^{-6}) \times (-4 \times 10^{-6})}{3^3} (-\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$

For reflected and refracted rays to be perpendicular, if $i$ is the angle of incidence and $r$ is the angle of refraction, then $i + r = 90°$, giving $r = 90° - i$.
Applying Snell's law: $n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r$
$2 \sin i = 2\sqrt{3} \sin(90° - i)$
$2 \sin i = 2\sqrt{3} \cos i$
$\tan i = \sqrt{3}$
$i = 60°$

47669.subject: Chemistry
47669.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I (Complex)List-II (Geometry)
(a)$[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$(i)Trigonal bipyramidal
(b)$[NiCl_4]^{2-}$(ii)Octahedral
(c)$[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$(iii)Tetrahedral
(d)$[Fe(CO)_5]$(iv)Square planar
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
47669.sol:
For $[\text{Co(NH}_3\text{)}_6]^{3+}$, the coordination number is $6$, which corresponds to an octahedral geometry. Thus, (a) matches with (ii).

For $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}$ is in the $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^8$ configuration. Since $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, no pairing occurs, leading to $sp^3$ hybridization and a tetrahedral geometry. Thus, (b) matches with (iii).

For $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}$ is in the $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^8$ configuration. Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, pairing of electrons occurs, leading to $dsp^2$ hybridization and a square planar geometry. Thus, (c) matches with (iv).

For $[\text{Fe(CO)}_5]$, the coordination number is $5$. $\text{Fe}$ is in the $0$ oxidation state with a $3d^6 4s^2$ configuration. The strong field ligand $\text{CO}$ causes pairing of electrons, resulting in $dsp^3$ hybridization and a trigonal bipyramidal geometry. Thus, (d) matches with (i).

The correct matching is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

Answer: a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i

The given expression is $\sum\limits_{n=1}^{4} (-1)^{2n} \cdot i^{2n}$

Expanding the sum for $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$:

49428.subject: Mathematics
49428.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are acute angles such that $\alpha - \beta$ and $\alpha + \beta$ satisfy the equation $\tan^2\theta - 4\tan\theta + 1 = 0$, then $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are respectively,
49428.sol:
The roots of the equation $\tan^2\theta - 4\tan\theta + 1 = 0$ are $\tan(\alpha - \beta)$ and $\tan(\alpha + \beta)$.

Sum of roots: $\tan(\alpha - \beta) + \tan(\alpha + \beta) = 4$

Product of roots: $\tan(\alpha - \beta) \tan(\alpha + \beta) = 1$

Using the tangent addition formula:

$\tan(2\alpha) = \tan((\alpha - \beta) + (\alpha + \beta)) = \dfrac{\tan(\alpha - \beta) + \tan(\alpha + \beta)}{1 - \tan(\alpha - \beta) \tan(\alpha + \beta)}$

Substituting the sum and product of roots:

$\tan(2\alpha) = \dfrac{4}{1 - 1} \rightarrow \infty$

Since $\alpha$ is an acute angle, $2\alpha = 90^{}^{\circ} \Rightarrow \alpha = 45^{}^{\circ}$.

Now, substituting $\alpha = 45^{}^{\circ}$ into the sum of roots equation:

$\tan(45^{}^{\circ} - \beta) + \tan(45^{}^{\circ} + \beta) = 4$

$\dfrac{1 - \tan\beta}{1 + \tan\beta} + \dfrac{1 + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\beta} = 4$

$\dfrac{(1 - \tan\beta)^2 + (1 + \tan\beta)^2}{1 - \tan^2\beta} = 4$

$\dfrac{2(1 + \tan^2\beta)}{1 - \tan^2\beta} = 4$

$1 + \tan^2\beta = 2 - 2\tan^2\beta$

$3\tan^2\beta = 1 \Rightarrow \tan\beta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ (since $\beta$ is acute)

Thus, $\beta = 30^{}^{\circ}$.

Answer: $45^{}^{\circ}, 30^{}^{\circ}$

56621.text: Identify species having metal atom in $+6$ oxidation state from following
56621.sol:
Let $x$ be the oxidation state of the metal atom in each species.

For $\text{MnO}_4^-$, the oxidation state of Mn is calculated as:

For $[\text{Cr}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$, the oxidation state of Cr is calculated as:
$x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$

For $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$, the oxidation state of Cr is calculated as:
$2x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$

For $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$, the oxidation state of Cr is calculated as:
$x + 2(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$

Thus, $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ has the metal atom in the $+6$ oxidation state.

57284.subject: Chemistry
57284.text: Which among the following is vinylic halide?
57284.sol:
Definition of Vinylic Halide: An organic compound where a halogen atom (X$) is bonded directly to an sp^2$ hybridized carbon that is part of a carbon–carbon double bond (C=C$).

A) Haloalkane: The halogen is bonded to an sp^3$ hybridized carbon, as in chloroethane (CH_3CH_2Cl$), which does not satisfy the definition.

B) Haloalkene: Includes structures where the halogen is attached to a carbon in an alkene. Vinylic halides (e.g., chloroethene, $CH_2=CH-Cl$) are a subset, with the halogen on an sp^2$ carbon of the double bond.

C) Haloalkyne: The halogen is bonded to an sp hybridized carbon in a triple bond, such as chloroethyne (CH\equiv C-Cl$), not meeting the criteria.

D) Haloarene: The halogen is on an sp^2$ carbon in an aromatic ring (e.g., chlorobenzene, $C_6H_5Cl$), but “vinylic” specifically denotes non-aromatic alkenes.

Thus, vinylic halides are a type of haloalkene, making B the correct classification.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

57568.subject: Chemistry
57568.text: Identify the product obtained when 2- Chloro - 2 - methylbutane is reacted with sodium metal in presence of dry ether?
57568.sol:
The given reactant is 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, which has the structure $CH_3-C(Cl)(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$.

When reacted with sodium metal in the presence of dry ether, it undergoes the Wurtz reaction.

The reaction proceeds via the formation of an alkyl free radical. The cleavage of the $C-Cl$ bond yields the radical $CH_3-C^{\bullet}(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$.

Two such radicals dimerize to form the final alkane product:

$2 CH_3-C(Cl)(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3 + 2 Na \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-C(CH_3)_2-CH_2-CH_3 + 2 NaCl$

The longest continuous carbon chain in the product contains 6 carbon atoms, making the parent chain a hexane. Numbering the chain from either end gives substituents at the 3rd and 4th positions.

There are four methyl groups attached to the main chain, two at C-3 and two at C-4. Thus, the IUPAC name of the product is $3,3,4,4-$tetramethylhexane.

57623.subject: Chemistry
57623.text:
Identify the product ' $X$ ' formed in the following reaction,
Sodium ethoxide + Isopropyl chloride $\longrightarrow X+$ Ethanol + Sodium Chloride
57623.sol:
Sodium ethoxide ($CH_3CH_2ONa$) is a strong base and nucleophile, while isopropyl chloride ($CH_3CHClCH_3$) is a secondary alkyl halide. This combination can lead to either substitution ($S_N2$) or elimination ($E2$) reactions.

In an $E2$ elimination, the ethoxide ion acts as a base, abstracting a $\beta$-hydrogen from the alkyl halide. The products are propene ($CH_2=CHCH_3$), ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$), and sodium chloride ($NaCl$). The formation of ethanol is characteristic of $E2$ elimination when ethoxide is the base.

A substitution pathway ($S_N2$) would yield 2-ethoxypropane without forming ethanol, which contradicts the given products. Among the options, only propene aligns with the $E2$ mechanism and observed byproducts.

The product $X$ is propene: $\boxed{C}$.

57752.subject: Chemistry
57752.text: Which of the following is NOT terminal alkyne ?
57752.sol:
Terminal alkynes have a triple bond at the end of the carbon chain, meaning at least one hydrogen atom is directly attached to a triply bonded carbon atom (R-C \equiv C-H$).

Ethyne is $H-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

Propyne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-1-yne is $CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-2-yne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$, where the triple bond is between the second and third carbon atoms. It does not have a hydrogen atom attached to the triply bonded carbon atoms. Thus, it is an internal alkyne, not a terminal alkyne.

Answer: But - 2 - yne$

59208.subject: Chemistry
59208.text: What is the relation between the vapour pressure of solution, vapour pressure of solvent and its mole fraction in the solution?
59208.sol:
The relation between the vapour pressure of the solution $\left(P_1\right)$, the vapour pressure of the pure solvent $\left(P_1^*\right)$, and the mole fraction of the solvent $\left(x_1\right)$ in the solution is given by Raoult's Law for an ideal solution.
Raoult's Law states: $P_1=P_1^* \cdot x_1$
Where: - $P_1$ is the vapour pressure of the solvent in the solution, - $P_1^*$ is the vapour pressure of the pure solvent, - $x_1$ is the mole fraction of the solvent in the solution. The correct relation is (1): $P_1=P_1^* \cdot x_1$

59865.subject: Chemistry
59865.text: Which from following is NOT a state function ?
59865.sol:
State functions are properties whose values depend only on the state of the system and are independent of the path followed to reach that state.

Pressure, volume, and temperature are state functions because they depend only on the initial and final states of the system.

Work and heat are path functions because their values depend on the specific path taken to go from the initial state to the final state.

Therefore, work is not a state function.

Answer: Work

60249.text: The function $\mathrm{f}(x)=x^3-6 x^2+a x+b$ satisfyies the conditions of Rolle's theorem in $[1,3]$. Then the values of $a$ and $b$ are respectively
60249.sol:
Rolle's Theorem requires $f(x)$ to be continuous on $[1,3]$, differentiable on $(1,3)$, and satisfy $f(1) = f(3)$.

Since $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + ax + b$ is a polynomial, continuity and differentiability are automatic.

Equating $f(1) = f(3)$:

$1 - 6 + a + b = 27 - 54 + 3a + b$
$a - 5 = 3a - 27$
$2a = 22$
$a = 11$

The only option with $a=11$ is A, implying $b=-6$.

With $a=11$, the derivative becomes $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 11$. Solving $f'(x)=0$ yields $x = 2 \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 1.423, 2.577$, both in $(1,3)$.

The values satisfying all conditions are $\boxed{A}$.

60684.subject: Mathematics
60684.sol:
Simplify the equation $\sqrt{\log_3 x^{16}} + 9 \log_{27} \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{x}} = 5$ using logarithmic properties. Apply the power rule to the first term: $\log_3 x^{16} = 16 \log_3 x$, so $\sqrt{\log_3 x^{16}} = 4\sqrt{\log_3 x}$.

Transform the base and argument in the second term:
$\log_{27} \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{x}} = \log_{3^3} \left(\frac{3}{x}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{1}{3} \log_3 \left(\frac{3}{x}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{1}{9} \log_3 \left(\frac{3}{x}\right)
Apply the quotient rule: \frac{1}{9} (\log_3 3 - \log_3 x) = \frac{1}{9}(1 - \log_3 x)$
Thus, $9 \log_{27} \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{x}$} = 1 - \log_3 x$.

The equation becomes 4\sqrt{\log_3 x} +1 - \log_3 x = 5$, requiring $\log_3 x \geq 0$ for the square root to be defined. Let $y = \sqrt{\log_3 x} with $ y \geq 0$, so \log_3 x = y²$.

Substituting yields $4y + 1 - y² = 5$, which simplifies to the quadratic equation $y^2 - 4y + 4 = 0$. Factoring gives $(y - 2)^2 = 0$, so $y = 2$.

Back-substitute: \sqrt{\log_3 x} =$2 \Rightarrow \log_3 x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 3^4 = 81$. Verification confirms this solution satisfies the original equation.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}$}$

$

63343.text: If the equation $\mathrm{k} x y+10 x+8 \mathrm{y}+16=0$ represents a pair of lines, then
options: the value of $k$ does not exist
63343.sol:
The condition for a second-degree equation $ax^2 + by^2 + 2hxy + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ to represent a pair of lines is $abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0$.

Comparing $kxy + 10x + 8y + 16 = 0$ with the general form yields:

$a = 0$, $b = 0$, $h = \frac{k}{2}$, $g = 5$, $f = 4$, $c = 16$

Substituting into the condition:

$(0)(0)(16) + 2(4)(5)\left(\frac{k}{2}\right) - (0)(4^2) - (0)(5^2) - 16\left(\frac{k}{2}\right)^2 = 0$

$20k - 4k^2 = 0$
$4k(5 - k) = 0$

The solutions are $k = 0$ and $k = 5$, both representing degenerate pairs of lines.

The final answer is $\boxed{C}$

65110.text: Let $(\bar{p} \wedge \bar{q})$ denote the angle between $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{q}$. If $\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c} = \bar{0}, |\bar{a}| = 7, |\bar{b}| = 5$ and $|\bar{c}| = 3$ then (take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
65110.sol:
Given $\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c} = \bar{0}$, we can write $\bar{a} + \bar{c} = -\bar{b}$.

Squaring both sides, we get:

$|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2 + 2|\bar{a}||\bar{c}|\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = |\bar{b}|^2$

Substituting the given values $|\bar{a}| = 7$, $|\bar{b}| = 5$, and $|\bar{c}| = 3$:

$7^2 + 3^2 + 2(7)(3)\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = 5^2$

$49 + 9 + 42\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = 25$

$58 + 42\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = 25$

$42\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -33$

$\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -\dfrac{33}{42} = -\dfrac{11}{14}$

Given $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$, we can rewrite the expression as:

$-\dfrac{11}{14} = -\dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{22}{7}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Therefore, $\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Answer: $\cos(\bar{a} \wedge \bar{c}) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

65127.subject: Mathematics
65127.sol:
Using the properties of the scalar triple product:

$[\bar{a}\ \ \bar{a} + \bar{b}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}] = [\bar{a}\ \ \bar{a}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}] + [\bar{a}\ \ \bar{b}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}]$

Since the scalar triple product is zero when two vectors are identical, $[\bar{a}\ \ \bar{a}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}] = 0$.

$[\bar{a}\ \ \bar{a} + \bar{b}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}] = [\bar{a}\ \ \bar{b}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}]$

This can be written as:

$[\bar{a}\ \ \bar{b}\ \ \bar{a} \times \bar{b}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) = |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2$

Using Lagrange's identity:

$|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{a}|^2 |\bar{b}|^2 - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})^2$

Substituting the given values $|\bar{a}| = 4$, $|\bar{b}| = 3$, and $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = 8$:

$|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2 = (4)^2 (3)^2 - (8)^2$

$|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2 = 16 \times 9 - 64$

$|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2 = 144 - 64 = 80$

Answer: $80$

69431.subject: Physics
69431.text: If p-n junction diode is forward biased then
69431.sol:
When a p-n junction diode is forward biased, the positive terminal of the external voltage source is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side.

The applied forward voltage opposes the built-in potential barrier, reducing the effective barrier voltage.

This external electric field pushes the majority charge carriers (holes in the p-region and electrons in the n-region) towards the junction.

As the carriers move towards the junction, they neutralize some of the immobile ions, which causes the width of the depletion layer to decrease.

This allows majority carriers to cross the junction easily, facilitating electric conduction.

Answer: width of depletion layer decreases.

70211.text: In Young's double slit experiment let 'd' be the distance between two slits and 'D' be the distance between the slits and the screen. Using a monochromatic source of wavelength ' $\lambda$ ', in an interference pattern, third minimum is observed exactly in front of one of the slits. If at the same point on the screen first minimum is to be obtained, the required change in the wavelength is [d & D are not changed]
70211.sol:
For a point directly in front of one slit, the path difference is $\Delta x = \frac{d^2}{2D}$, since $y = d/2$ from the central maximum.

The condition for the third minimum requires $\frac{d^2}{2D} = \frac{5}{2}\lambda$, so $\frac{d^2}{D} = 5\lambda$.

For the first minimum to occur at the same position with a new wavelength $\lambda'$, the path difference gives $\frac{d^2}{2D} = \frac{1}{2}\lambda'$, so $\frac{d^2}{D} = \lambda'$.

Equating, $\lambda' = 5\lambda$, and the change required is $\Delta\lambda = 4\lambda$.

70845.text: A body of mass 1 kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F}=\left(t \hat{i}+2 t^2 \hat{j}\right) N$, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are unit vectors along $x$ and $y$ axis. The power developed by above force at time $t=3$ second will be
70845.sol:
Given: Mass $m = 1 \text{ kg}$ and force $\vec{F} = (t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j}) \text{ N}$. The power developed by the force is $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}$.

Applying Newton's second law, acceleration is $\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j} \text{ m/s}^2$. Since the body starts from rest, velocity is found by integrating acceleration: $\vec{v} = \int (t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j}) \, dt = \left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) \hat{i} + \left(\frac{2t^3}{3}\right) \hat{j} \text{ m/s}$.

Power is then calculated as $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (t \hat{i} + 2t^2 \hat{j}) \cdot \left(\frac{t^2}{2} \hat{i} + \frac{2t^3}{3} \hat{j}\right) = \frac{t^3}{2} + \frac{4t^5}{3}$.

At $t = 3$, $P(3) = \frac{27}{2} + \frac{4 \times 243}{3} = 13.5 + 324 = 337.5 \text{ W}$.

72114.text: A parallel-plate air capacitor has a capacity '$C$', distance with a separation '$x$', a dielectric material with a dielectric constant '$k$' between plates, and a potential difference with a '$V$' volt applied between plates. The force of attraction between the plates is

The capacitance of the air capacitor is given by $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{x}$, where $A$ is the area of the plates.

When a dielectric material of dielectric constant $k$ is introduced between the plates, the new capacitance becomes $C' = kC$.

The charge on the capacitor plates when a potential difference $V$ is applied is $Q = C'V = kCV$.

The magnitude of the force of attraction between the plates of the capacitor is given by $F = \dfrac{Q^2}{2k\epsilon_0 A}$.

Substituting $Q = kCV$ and $\epsilon_0 A = Cx$, we get:

$F = \dfrac{(kCV)^2}{2k(Cx)}$

$F = \dfrac{k^2C^2V^2}{2kCx}$

$F = \dfrac{kCV^2}{2x}$

Answer: $\dfrac{kCV^2}{2x}$

73809.subject: General Ability
73809.text: In which cell does the first meiotic cell division take place during the process of spermatogenesis?
73809.sol:
During spermatogenesis, the spermatogonia present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules multiply by mitotic division and increase in numbers. Some of the spermatogonia, called primary spermatocytes, periodically undergo meiosis.

A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to the formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes.

The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids.

Answer: Primary spermatocyte

73848.subject: General Ability
73848.text: What happens when the sunlight travels through the Earth's atmosphere?
options: The blue colour is scattered more compared to the red colour
The red colour is scattered more compared to the blue colour
Both the blue and the red colours are scattered equally
The blue colour is not scattered but the red colour is scattered the most
73848.sol:
According to Rayleigh scattering, the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of its wavelength, given by $I \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda^4}$.

Since the wavelength of blue light is shorter than the wavelength of red light ($\lambda_{\text{blue}} < \lambda_{\text{red}}$), blue light is scattered much more strongly by the molecules in the Earth's atmosphere compared to red light.

Therefore, the blue colour is scattered more compared to the red colour.

Answer: The blue colour is scattered more compared to the red colour

73904.subject: General Ability
73904.text: Which one of the following instruments can be used to measure −250°C temperature?
options: By using a mercury based thermometer
By using an alcohol based thermometer
73904.sol:
Mercury freezes at $-39^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$, so a mercury-based thermometer cannot be used to measure $-250^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Alcohol freezes at $-115^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$, so an alcohol-based thermometer is also unsuitable for measuring $-250^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.

A clinical thermometer is designed to measure human body temperature, typically in the narrow range of $35^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $42^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.

A thermocouple-based thermometer can measure a very wide range of temperatures, typically from $-270^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ to over $2000^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ depending on the metals used. Therefore, it can be used to measure $-250^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Answer: By using thermocouple based thermometer

83103.subject: Physics
83103.text: The following plots show variation of velocity ($v$) with time ($t$), of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Which of the following plots is/are correct ?
83103.sol:
Let the upward direction be considered positive.

When a ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity $u$, it moves under the constant downward acceleration due to gravity ($a = -g$).

The velocity $v$ at any time $t$ is given by the kinematic equation:
$v = u + at$
$\Rightarrow v = u - gt$

This equation represents a straight line with a positive y-intercept ($u$) and a constant negative slope ($-g$).

Initially, the velocity is positive and decreases linearly until it becomes zero at the highest point. As the ball falls back down, the velocity becomes negative and its magnitude increases linearly.

Plot C correctly shows a straight line starting from a positive value on the v-axis, crossing the t-axis, and continuing with a constant negative slope.

Answer: C only

84639.subject: Zoology
84639.text: The amnion of mammalian embryo is derived from
84639.sol:
Amnion, in reptiles, birds, and mammals, is a membrane forming a fluid-filled cavity (the amniotic sac) that encloses the embryo. The amniotic sac and the fluid it contains are sometimes referred to as the bag of waters.
In development, the amnion arises by the folding of a mass of extra-embryonic tissue called the somatopleure. Lined with ectoderm and covered with mesoderm (both are germ layers), the amnion contains a thin, transparent fluid in which the embryo is suspended, thus providing a cushion against mechanical injury. The amnion also provides protection against fluid loss from the embryo itself and against tissue adhesions.

84706.text:
Select the correct statements regarding mechanism of muscle contraction.
A. It is initiated by a signal sent by CNS via sensory neuron.
B. Neurotransmitter generates action potential in the sarcolemma.
C. Increased $\mathrm{Ca}^{++}$level leads to the binding of calcium with troponin on action filaments.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
84706.sol: The correct answer is option (1) as muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the CNS via a motor neuron. A neural signal reaching the neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2 *}$ into the sarcoplasm. Increase in $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin on actin filaments and thereby remove the masking of active sites for myosin. Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head now binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.

85555.text: In which one of the following preparations are you likely to come across cell junctions most frequently?
85555.sol:

The other three (thrombocytes, tendon and hyaline cartilage) belongs to connective tissue. Thrombocytes or platelets aid the formation of blood clots by releasing various protein substances. Tendon attaches a muscle to a bone and hyaline cartilage gives flexibility and support at the joints.

86804.subject: Physics
86804.text: The angular speed of the Earth's rotation is $7.3 \times 10^{-5}$ rad\cdot s^{-1}$. Take the radius of the Earth at the equator to be 6400$ km. Then the ratio $(a_c/g)$ of the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration $a_c$ at a point on the equator to $g$, is of the order
86804.sol:
Given angular speed $\omega = 7.3 \times 10^{-5}$ rad$\cdot$ s^{-1}$ and radius $R = 6400$ km $= 6.4 \times 10^6$ m.

The centripetal acceleration at the equator is:

$a_c = \omega^2 R$

$a_c = (7.3 \times 10^{-5})^2 \times (6.4 \times 10^6)$

$a_c \approx 53.29 \times 10^{-10} \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \approx 3.41 \times 10^{-2}$ m$\cdot$ s^{-2}$

Taking acceleration due to gravity $g \approx 9.8$ m$\cdot$ s^{-2}$, the ratio is:

\dfrac{a_c}{g} = \dfrac{3.41 \times 10^{-2}}{9.8} \approx 3.48 \times 10^{-3}$

The order of magnitude of this ratio is $10^{-3}$.

Answer: $10^{-3}$

87814.subject: Chemistry
87814.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
87814.text:
The correct decreasing order of electropositive character among the following elements is :

Fe, Sc, Rb, Br, Te, F, Ca
options: Fe > Sc > Rb > Br > Te > F > Ca
Ca > Rb > Sc > Fe > Te > F > Br
Rb > Ca > Sc > Fe > Br > Te > F
Rb > Ca > Sc > Fe > Te > Br > F
87814.sol:
(i)& Alkali and alkaline earth metals are most electro-positive. Alkali metals are more electropositive than alkaline earth metals.

(ii)& In d-block series, the elements near alkaline earth metals are more electropositive than rest of the members.

(iii)& Metalloids are less electropositive than metals.

(iv) Halogens (Non-metals) are least electropositive. In halogen group, electropositive character increases as atomic number increases.

89762.subject: Mathematics
89762.text: The denominator of a fraction exceeds the square of the numerator by 16, then the least value of the fraction is
89762.sol:
Let the numerator be $x$, then $\text{f} \left(\text{x}\right) = \dfrac{\text{x}}{x^{2} + 1 6}$

On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get

$f^{′} \left(\text{x}\right) = \dfrac{\left(x^{2} + 1 6\right) \cdot 1 - \text{x} \left(2 \text{x}\right)}{{\left(x^{2} + 1 6\right)}^{2}}$

$= \dfrac{x^{2} + 1 6 - 2 x^{2}}{{\left(x^{2} + 1 6\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{1 6 - x^{2}}{{\left(x^{2} + 1 6\right)}^{2}}$...(i)

Putting $f^{'} ( x ) = 0$ for maxima or minima, we get,

$16 - x^{2} = 0 ⇒ x = 4, - 4$
Again, on differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get

$f^{″} \left(\text{x}\right) = \dfrac{{\left(x^{2} + 1 6\right)}^{2} - \left(- 2 \text{x}\right) - \left(1 6 - x^{2}\right)^{2} \left(x^{2} + 1 6\right)^{2} \text{x}}{{\left(x^{2} + 1 6\right)}^{4}}$

At $x = 4, f^{"} ( x ) < 0$

∴ $f ( x )$ is maximum at $x = 4$

And at $x = - 4, f^{"} ( x ) > 0 ⇒ f ( x )$ is minimum

∴ Least value of $\text{f} \left(\text{x}\right) = \dfrac{- 4}{1 6 + 1 6} = - \dfrac{1}{8}$
&

91723.text: If both the roots of the equation $x^{2} + \left(a - 1\right)x + a = 0$ are positive, then the complete solution set of real values of $a$& is
91723.sol:
Both roots are positive $⇒ D > 0, S > 0, P > 0$
Sum of the roots, $S > 0 ⇒ - \left(a - 1\right) > 0 ⇒ a - 1 < 0 ⇒ a < 1$
Product of roots, $P > 0 ⇒ a > 0$
Discriminant, $D > 0 ⇒ {\left(a - 1\right)}^{2} - 4a > 0 ⇒ a^{2} + 1 - 6a > 0$

$a^{2} - 6a + 1 > 0 ⇒ a > 3 + 2\sqrt{2}$ or $a < 3 - 2\sqrt{2}$
Taking intersection we get $a \in \left(0,3 - $2\sqrt{2}\right)

93266.subject: Physics
93266.text: In older times, people used to think that the Earth was flat. Imagine that the Earth is indeed not a sphere of radius $R$, but an infinite plate of thickness $H$. What value of $H$ is needed to allow the same gravitational acceleration to be experienced as on the surface of the actual Earth? (Assume that the Earth's density is uniform and equal in the two models).
93266.sol:
Applying Gauss law

$∮ \overset{→}{E} . d\overset{→}{s} = 4\piG{m}_{in}$

Where $\overset{→}{E}$ is gravitational field at $d\overset{→}{s}$

Computing over colsed surface given

$E2s = 4\piG( ρsh )$

$E = \dfrac{4\piGρh}{2}$ ... (1)

On the surface of earth with radius $R$, $E = \dfrac{G( ρ\dfrac{4}{3} \piR^{3} )}{R^{2}}$

$= Gρ\dfrac{4}{3} \piR$ ... (2)

Equating (1) and (2)

$\dfrac{4\piGρh}{2} = Gρ\dfrac{4}{3} \piR$

$h = \dfrac{2R}{3}$

93269.text: A body weighs $W$ at the surface of the earth. Its weight at a height equal to half the radius of the earth will be
93269.sol:
The weight of an object at the surface of the earth is

$W = mg = m\dfrac{GM}{R2}$

At a height $h = \dfrac{R}{2}$, the weight would be

$W^{'} = m\dfrac{GM}{\left(R + h\right)^{2}} = \dfrac{4}{9} \times m\dfrac{GM}{R2}$

$∴ W^{'} = \dfrac{4}{9}W$

In addition to proteins viruses also contain genetic material, that could be either RNA or DNA. In general, viruses that infect plants have single stranded RNA. If the electrons are sharing between the two same kinds of atoms then it will form a non-polar molecule. Eg:- ${H}_{2,}{N}_{2,}and{F}_{2}etc.$

If the sharing of electrons between the two different kinds of elements then the more electronegative element attracts shared pair of electrons towards itself and gets the partial negative charge corresponding the less electronegative atom carries the partial positive charge. 101942.text: The coefficient of volume expansion of glycerine is $49 \times 10^{-50} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$. What is the fractional change in density for a $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ rise in temperature?
101942.sol:
Here, $\gamma=49 \times 19^{-5}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$
$\begin{aligned} \Delta \mathrm{T} & =30^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{V}^{\prime} & =\mathrm{V}+\Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{l}+\gamma \Delta \mathrm{T})\end{aligned}$
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}^{\prime}=\mathrm{V}\left(1+49 \times 10^{-5} \times 30\right)=1.0147 \mathrm{~V}$
$\because \quad \rho=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{V}}$ and $\rho^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{V}^{\prime}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{0.0147}=0.9855 \rho$
Hence, fractional change in density
$=\frac{\rho-\rho^{\prime}}{\rho}=\frac{\rho-0.9855 \rho}{\rho}=0.0145$

102937.subject: Physics
102937.text: Two point charges $+2 \mu\text{C}$ and $-2 \mu\text{C}$ are placed at the coordinates $(0, 2\text{ cm}, 0)$ and $(0, -2\text{ cm}, 0)$ respectively. If this electric dipole is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec{E} = 5 \times 10^5 \hat{i}\text{ N C}^{-1}$, what is the torque vector experienced by the dipole?
102937.sol:
The electric dipole moment $\vec{p}$ is a vector directed from the negative charge to the positive charge.

Position of $-q$ is $(0, -2\text{ cm}, 0)$ and position of $+q$ is $(0, 2\text{ cm}, 0)$.
The displacement vector $\vec{d}$ from $-q$ to $+q$ is:
$\vec{d} = (2 - (-2))\hat{j}\text{ cm} = 4\hat{j}\text{ cm} = 0.04\hat{j}\text{ m}$

The dipole moment $\vec{p}$ is:
$\vec{p} = q\vec{d} = (2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}) \times (0.04\hat{j}\text{ m}) = 8 \times 10^{-8}\hat{j}\text{ C m}$

The electric field is given as $\vec{E} = 5 \times 10^5 \hat{i}\text{ N C}^{-1}$.

The torque $\vec{\tau}$ experienced by the dipole is the cross product of $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{E}$:
$\vec{\tau} = \vec{p} \times \vec{E}$
$\vec{\tau} = (8 \times 10^{-8}\hat{j}) \times (5 \times 10^5 \hat{i})$
$\vec{\tau} = (8 \times 5 \times 10^{-3}) (\hat{j} \times \hat{i})$
$\vec{\tau} = 40 \times 10^{-3} (-\hat{k})\text{ N m}$
$\vec{\tau} = -0.04 \hat{k}\text{ N m}$

Answer: $-0.04 \hat{k}\text{ N m}$

107715.subject: Chemistry
107715.text: Which of the following molecules possesses lone pairs on its central atom but has a zero dipole moment due to its symmetrical planar shape?
107715.sol:
In $\text{BrF}_5$, the central Br atom has 7 valence electrons. It forms 5 bonds and has 1 lone pair. The shape is square pyramidal, which is asymmetric, making the molecule polar ($\mu \neq 0$).

In $\text{XeF}_4$, the central Xe atom has 8 valence electrons. It forms 4 bonds and has 2 lone pairs. The electron geometry is octahedral, and the two lone pairs occupy opposite (trans) positions to minimize repulsion. This results in a symmetrical square planar shape. The bond dipoles cancel each other out, giving a zero dipole moment ($\mu = 0$).

In $\text{SF}_4$, the central S atom has 6 valence electrons. It forms 4 bonds and has 1 lone pair. The shape is see-saw, which is asymmetric, making the molecule polar ($\mu \neq 0$).

In $\text{CCl}_4$, the central C atom has 4 valence electrons and forms 4 bonds with no lone pairs. While it has a zero dipole moment, it lacks lone pairs on the central atom.

Answer: $\text{XeF}_4$

109376.subject: Chemistry
109376.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ ($K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}$) is more soluble in water than $\text{AgCl}$ ($K_{sp} = 1.0 \times 10^{-10}$).
Reason (R): For sparingly soluble salts, a higher numerical value of $K_{sp}$ always implies a higher molar solubility.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
109376.sol:
Let $s$ be the molar solubility.

For $\text{AgCl}$ (an AB type salt):
$K_{sp} = s^2$
$s = \sqrt{1.0 \times 10^{-10}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$

For $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ (an $\text{A}_2\text{B}$ type salt):
$K_{sp} = (2s)^2(s) = 4s^3$
$4s^3 = 3.2 \times 10^{-11} = 32 \times 10^{-12}$
$s^3 = 8.0 \times 10^{-12}$
$s = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ M}$

Comparing the solubilities, $2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ M} > 1.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$. Thus, $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ is more soluble than $\text{AgCl}$, making the Assertion (A) correct.

The Reason (R) is incorrect because $K_{sp}$ values can only be directly compared to determine relative solubilities if the salts have the same stoichiometry. As shown here, $\text{AgCl}$ has a higher $K_{sp}$ ($10^{-10} > 10^{-11}$) but a lower molar solubility.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

110667.text: Which one of the following compounds is a peroxide?
110667.sol:
Key Idea:- In peroxides, the oxidation state of $O$ is - 1 and they give $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$, with dilute acids, and have peroxide linkage.
In $\mathrm{KO}_2$,

+1+($\mathrm{x} \times$2)=0

In $\mathrm{BaO}_2$,

$\begin{aligned}$& +2+($\mathrm{x} \times$2)=0 \\
& $\mathrm{x}=-$1
\end{aligned}

Thus, it is a peroxide. Only it$ gives \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ when reacts with dilute acids and has peroxide linkage as

$\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}[\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}]^{2-}$\\
& $\text{ peroxide linkage }
\end{aligned}$In $\mathrm{MnO}_2$ and $\mathrm{NO}_2, \mathrm{Mn} and \mathrm{N}$ exhibit variable oxidation states, thus, the oxidation state of $O$ in these is -2 . Hence, these are not peroxides. Thus, it is clear, that among the given molecules only $\mathrm{BaO}_2$ is a peroxide.

120972.subject: Chemistry
120972.text: A researcher heats an aqueous solution of a globular protein. Upon analysis, it is observed that the protein has lost its biological activity and its helical structures have uncoiled, but the sequence of amino acids remains perfectly intact. Identify the phenomenon that has occurred and the primary type of bond that was disrupted during this process.
120972.sol:
When a protein is subjected to physical changes such as heating, the hydrogen bonds holding the secondary and tertiary structures are disturbed. This causes the uncoiling of helices and unfolding of globules, leading to a loss of biological activity.

This phenomenon is known as denaturation. Since the sequence of amino acids remains intact, the primary structure is preserved, which means the covalent peptide bonds are not broken during this process. Therefore, the phenomenon is denaturation and the disrupted bonds are hydrogen bonds.

Answer: Denaturation and Hydrogen bonds

123206.subject: Botany
123206.text: What are the cells that become specialised in shape and size in the vicinity of the guard cells called?
123206.sol: The epidermal tissue system forms the outer-most covering of the whole plant body and comprises epidermal cells, stomata and the epidermal appendages – the trichomes and hairs. The epidermis is the outermost layer of the primary plant body. It is made up of elongated, compactly arranged cells, which form a continuous layer. Epidermis is usually single-Layered. Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole. The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle which prevents the loss of water. Cuticle is absent in roots. Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata. Sometimes, a few epidermal cells, in the vicinity of the guard cells become specialised in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells. The stomatal aperture, guard cells and the surrounding subsidiary cells are together called stomatal apparatus The cells of epidermis bear a number of hairs. The root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals On the stem the epidermal hairs are called trichomes. The trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular They may be branched or unbranched and soft or stiff. They may even be secretory. The trichomes help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

124978.subject: Botany
124978.text: Where does the complete oxidation of pyruvate take place within the mitochondria?
124978.sol:
For aerobic respiration to take place within the mitochondria, the final product of glycolysis, pyruvate is transported from the cytoplasm into the mitochondria. The crucial events in aerobic respiration are:

• The complete oxidation of pyruvate by the stepwise removal of all the hydrogen atoms, leaving three molecules of CO2 .

• The passing on of the electrons removed as part of the hydrogen atoms to molecular O2 with simultaneous synthesis of ATP.

What is interesting to note is that the first process takes place in the matrix of the mitochondria while the second process is located on the inner membrane of the mitochondria

125179.subject: Botany
125179.text: In plants, sucrose is broken down by the enzyme invertase to yield two monosaccharides that enter the glycolytic pathway. When one molecule of sucrose is respired, what is the total number of ATP molecules utilized in the phosphorylation steps of glycolysis before the cleavage of the 6-carbon sugars occurs?
125179.sol:
According to NCERT, sucrose is converted into glucose and fructose by the enzyme invertase, and both these monosaccharides readily enter the glycolytic pathway.

Each hexose molecule (glucose or fructose) requires the utilization of two ATP molecules during the preparatory (phosphorylation) phase of glycolysis:
1. First ATP is utilized when the sugar is phosphorylated by hexokinase.
2. Second ATP is utilized in the conversion of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.

Since one molecule of sucrose yields two hexose molecules (one glucose and one fructose), the total number of ATP molecules utilized is 2 \(\times\) 2 = 4.

Students often mistakenly choose 2 by forgetting that sucrose is a disaccharide that yields two monosaccharides, or 8 by confusing ATP utilization with gross ATP production.

Answer: 4

125341.subject: Botany
125341.text: What is the color of chlorophyll a in the chromatogram?
125341.sol: Looking at plants have you ever wondered why and how there are so many shades of green in their leaves – even in the same plant? We can look for an answer to this question by trying to separate the leaf pigments of any green plant through paper chromatography. A chromatographic separation of the leaf pigments shows that the colour that we see in leaves is not due to a single pigment but due to four pigments: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue green in the chromatogram), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Let us now see what roles various pigments play in photosynthesis.

128395.subject: Zoology
128395.text: What happens when a hormone binds to its receptor?
options: No changes occur in the target tissue
Target tissue metabolism and hence physiological functions are regulated
128395.sol: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors (present in the nucleus). Binding of a hormone to its receptor leads to the formation of a hormone-receptor complex (Figure 19.5 a, b). Each receptor is specific to one hormone only and hence receptors are specific. Hormone-Receptor complex formation leads to certain biochemical changes in the target tissue. Target tissue metabolism and hence physiological functions are regulated by hormones. Hormones which interact with membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell, but generate second messengers (e.g., cyclic AMP, IP3, Ca++ etc) which in turn regulate cellular metabolism (Figure 19.5a). Hormones which interact with intracellular receptors (e.g., steroid hormones, iodothyronines, etc.) mostly regulate gene expression or chromosome function by the interaction of hormone-receptor complex with the genome. Cumulative biochemical actions result in physiological and developmental effects (Figure 19.5b).

128896.text: What is the definition of cardiac output?
options: The volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute
The number of beats per minute

128896.sol: consists of systole and diastole of both the atria and ventricles. As mentioned earlier, the heart beats 72 times per minute, i.e., that many cardiac cycles are performed per minute. From this it could be deduced that the duration of a cardiac cycle is 0.8 seconds. During a cardiac cycle, each ventricle pumps out approximately 70 mL of blood which is called the stroke volume. The stroke volume multiplied by the heart rate (no. of beats per min.) gives the cardiac output. Therefore, the cardiac output can be defined as the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute and averages 5000 mL or 5 litres in a healthy individual. The body has the ability to alter the stroke volume as well as the heart rate and thereby the cardiac output.

129582.subject: Zoology
129582.text: What is the purpose of the dialysing fluid used in hemodialysis?
options: To remove glucose from the blood
To remove urea from the blood
To have the same composition as plasma
To remove bilirubin from the blood
129582.sol: Malfunctioning of kidneys can lead to accumulation of urea in blood, a condition called uremia, which is highly harmful and may lead to kidney failure. In such patients, urea can be removed by a process called hemodialysis. During the process of haemodialysis, the blood drained from a convenient artery is pumped into a dialysing unit called artificial kidney.. Blood drained from a convenient artery is pumped into a dialysing unit after adding an anticoagulant like heparin. The unit contains a coiled cellophane tube surrounded by a fluid (dialysing fluid) having the same composition as that of plasma except the nitrogenous wastes. The porous cellophane membrane of the tube allows the passage of molecules based on concentration gradient. As nitrogenous wastes are absent in the dialysing fluid, these substances freely move out, thereby clearing the blood. The cleared blood is pumped back to the body through a vein after adding anti-heparin to it. This method is a boon for thousands of uremic patients all over the world.

129787.subject: Zoology
129787.text: How do reptiles, birds, and mammals respire?
129787.sol: Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange O2 with CO2 by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. Earthworms use their moist cuticle and insects have a network of tubes (tracheal tubes) to transport atmospheric air within the body. Special vascularized structures called gills (branchial respiration) are used by most of the aquatic arthropods and molluscs whereas vascularised bags called lungs (pulmonary respiration) are used by the terrestrial forms for the exchange of gases. Among vertebrates, fishes use gills whereas amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals respire through lungs. Amphibians like frogs can respire through their moist skin (cutaneous respiration) also.

131336.subject: Zoology
131336.text: Which one of the following is an environmentrelated disorder with the correct main cause ?
options: Black lung disease (pneumoconiosis) found mainly in workers in stone quarries and crushers.
Blue baby disease (methaemoglobinaemia) due to heavy use of nitrogenous fertilizers in the area.
Non-hodgkin's lymphoma found mainly in workers involved in manufacture of neem based pesticides.
Skin cancer mainly in people exposed to benzene and methane.
131336.sol:
Blue baby syndrome is a pathological condition, called methemoglobinemia, in which blood's capacity for oxygen transport is reduced, resulting in bluish skin discoloration in infants. Blue baby syndrome begins when large amounts of nitrates in water are ingested by an infant and converted to nitrite by the digestive system. The nitrite then reacts with oxyhaemoglobin (the oxygen-carrying blood protein) to form metheglobin, which cannot carry oxygen.
Pneumoconiosis is a man-made, occupational lung diseases that are contracted by prolonged breathing of coal mine dust i.e. caused by the inhalation of dust, characterized by formation of nodular fibrotic changes in lungs.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (or NHL) is a cancer of lymphoid tissue, a part of the lymphatic system. NHL is a heterogenous disease.
Skin cancer is a malignant tumor that grows in the skin cells. It is commonly caused by exposure to the sun's UV rays.

131658.text: Select the correct statement for the given figure.

Since DNA from every tissue, from an individual shows the same degree of polymorphism, they become a very useful identification tool in forensic applications.
As the polymorphisms are not inheritable from parents to children, DNA fingerprinting is the basis of paternity testing, in case of disputes.
131658.sol: The bulk DNA forms a major peak and the other small peaks are referred to as satellite DNA. Depending on base composition (A : T rich or G:C rich), length of segment, and number of repetitive units, the satellite DNA is classified into many categories, such as micro-satellites, mini-satellites etc. These sequences normally do not code for any proteins, but they form a large portion of the human genome. These sequences show a high degree of polymorphism and form the basis of DNA fingerprinting. Since DNA from every tissue (such as blood, hair-follicle, skin, bone, saliva, sperm etc.), if an individual shows the same degree of polymorphism, they become a very useful identification tool in forensic applications. Further, as the polymorphisms are inheritable from parents to children, DNA fingerprinting is the basis of paternity testing, in case of disputes.

131795.subject: Zoology
131795.text: Read the following statements regarding the structural gene in a transcription unit and choose the incorrect one.
options: In eukaryotes, the coding sequences or expressed sequences within a structural gene are defined as introns.
The structural gene in a transcription unit is flanked by the promoter and terminator regions.
In eukaryotes, the structural gene is mostly monocistronic.
In bacteria or prokaryotes, the structural gene is predominantly polycistronic.
131795.sol:
In eukaryotes, the coding sequences or expressed sequences are defined as exons, not introns. Introns are intervening sequences that do not appear in mature or processed RNA.

The structural gene in a transcription unit is indeed flanked by the promoter (towards the $5'$ end of the coding strand) and the terminator (towards the $3'$ end). Furthermore, eukaryotic structural genes are mostly monocistronic, whereas prokaryotic structural genes are predominantly polycistronic. Therefore, the statement regarding introns being coding sequences is the incorrect one.

Answer: In eukaryotes, the coding sequences or expressed sequences within a structural gene are defined as introns.

131842.subject: Zoology
131842.text:
Read the following statements regarding the methodologies of the Human Genome Project:

(I) The Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) approach focuses on sequencing the whole set of genome containing all the coding and non-coding sequences.
(II) Sequence annotation involves sequencing the entire genome and later assigning different regions in the sequence with functions.
(III) Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) identify all the genes that are expressed as RNA.
(IV) The blind approach of simply sequencing the whole set of genome is called Expressed Sequence Tags.

How many of the above statements are correct?
131842.sol:
Statement (I) is incorrect because sequencing the whole set of genome containing all the coding and non-coding sequences is the approach known as Sequence Annotation, not Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs).

Statement (II) is correct as Sequence Annotation involves sequencing the entire genome and later assigning different regions in the sequence with functions.

Statement (III) is correct as ESTs specifically focus on identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA.

Statement (IV) is incorrect because the blind approach of simply sequencing the whole set of genome is called Sequence Annotation, not ESTs.

Therefore, exactly two statements, (II) and (III), are correct.

Answer: Two

132674.subject: Zoology
132674.text: Who else, besides Darwin, came to similar conclusions about natural selection around the same time?
132674.sol: Those characteristics which enable some to survive better in natural conditions (climate, food, physical factors, etc.) would outbreed others that are less-endowed to survive under such natural conditions. Another word used is fitness of the individual or population. The fitness, according to Darwin, refers ultimately and only to reproductive fitness. Hence, those who are better fit in an environment, leave more progeny than others. These, therefore, will survive more and hence are selected by nature. He called it natural selection and implied it as a mechanism of evolution. Alfred Wallace, a naturalist who worked in the Malay Archipelago had also come to similar conclusions around the same time. In due course of time, apparently new types of organisms are recognisable. All the existing life forms share similarities and share common ancestors. However, these ancestors were present at different periods in the history of earth (epochs, periods and eras). The geological history of earth closely correlates with the biological history of earth. A common permissible conclusion is that earth is very old, not thousand of years as was thought earlier but billions of years old.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sweet potato and potato represent convergent evolution.
Reason (R): They share a similar anatomical origin and structure but perform different functions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
132936.sol:
Sweet potato is a root modification and potato is a stem modification. They have different anatomical origins but perform the same function of food storage. This makes them analogous organs, which are a result of convergent evolution. Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) is incorrect because analogous organs have different anatomical origins and perform similar functions. The statement in the reason describes homologous organs (divergent evolution), not analogous ones.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

133123.sol: Hugo de Vries (1848-1935) proposed mutation theory for the formation of new species. According to him, new species are not formed by continuous variations but by sudden appearance of variations which he assigned as mutations. He stated that these mutations are heritable and persist in successive generations. For proposing this theory he performed experiments on Oenothera lamarckiana (evening primrose).

133793.text: How does the use of weedicides affect our soil?
options: They do not affect the soil
133793.sol: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests. In modern society, these problems have been tackled increasingly by the use of chemicals – by use of insecticides and pesticides. These chemicals are toxic and extremely harmful, to human beings and animals alike, and have been polluting our environment (soil, ground water), fruits, vegetables and crop plants. Our soil is also polluted through our use of weedicides to remove weeds.

133824.subject: Zoology
133824.text: What are the sources of biofertilisers?
133824.sol: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil. The main sources of biofertilisers are bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria. Also the nodules on the roots of leguminous plants formed by the symbiotic association of Rhizobium. These bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms, which is used by the plant as nutrient. Other bacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil (examples Azospirillum and Azotobacter), thus enriching the nitrogen content of the soil.
